text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- The cabinet approved a package of proposals essentially meeting the demands made by demonstrating farmers this week, as protests continued across Hungary. The Farmers Federation and the Peasants' Federation are organising a nationwide protest for March 10.
- The cabinet authorised Transport Minister Karoly Lotz to hold talks with operators of the M5 toll highway to Kecskemet on the possibility of lowering the HUF 850 toll.
- Visiting German President Roman Herzog wound up his three-day official visit by touring eastern Hungary to "rivet attention on the eastern region of Hungary".

- EBRD will invest ECU 30 million into promising but capital-hungry Hungarian companies in the next five years, programme manager Szabolcs Szekeres announced yesterday. A further ECU 5.4 million will be added by the EU's Phare programme.
- Democratic Forum president Sandor Lezsak met the ambassadors of the EU countries accredited to Budapest yesterday.
- The $103 million credit agreement on the development of Ferihegy Airport terminal 2B was signed yesterday.
- The aluminum oxide factory Almasfuzitoi Timfoldgyar will be closed down for the second time in the past three years, company management and unions agreed yesterday.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Residents of towns near the M5 motorway connecting the capital and Kecskemet reiterated their threat yesterday to partially block the highway on March 9 if the government does not give in to their demands.
- The far-right Hungarian Justice and Life Party MIEP held a rally outside Parliament yesterday to express support with the demonstrating farmers.
- The World Wildlife Fund said in a report that tremendous ecological damage has been inflicted along both sides of the Hungarian-Slovak border along the river Danube.
NEPSZAVA
- President Petar Stoyanov of Bulgaria arrives in Budapest tomorrow on an official visit to Hungary.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The Hungarian bond market stabilised in yesterday's auction as there was very little change from last week on the yields of three securities offered yesterday.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The City of Budapest approved its 1997 budget yesterday, projecting a deficit of HUF 21.39 billion.

- The international road show of the shares of the agricultural machinery producer Mezogep was a roaring success, as investors oversubscribed the package by 900 percent, said Zoltan Fekete of Credit Suisse First Boston.
- Of the four regional electricity distribution firms who have published their results only Demasz was profitable last year.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- In 1997, the foodstuff and household products retailer Spar plans to repeat last year's performance of boosting its revenue by 60 percent to HUF 30 billion.
-- Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
